test_title: PYST 5 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 13 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "minute" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence?

"The microscope revealed a minute speck of dust"

options.text: The meeting will start in a few minutes.
I was just a minute away from being late.
The camera captured every minute detail of the insect’s wing.
The alarm went off in exactly sixty seconds, or one minute.

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. The camera captured every minute detail of the insect’s wing .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"minute"** in the given sentence refers to something **extremely small** or **tiny**.
 
• Option 3 uses the word "minute" with the same meaning, emphasizing the **tiny details** captured by the camera.
 
• Other options, such as 1, 2, and 4, refer to "minute" as a unit of time, which is not the intended meaning in the given sentence.

Correct sentence: *The camera captured every minute detail of the insect’s wing.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word "minute" has two distinct meanings:
 
 
• **Time-related:** Refers to a unit of time equivalent to 60 seconds (e.g., "The meeting will start in a few minutes").
 
• **Size-related:** Refers to something extremely small or detailed (e.g., "A minute speck of dust").
 
 
 
• Understanding the context of the sentence is crucial to determining the correct meaning of the word.
